subject: IB Environmental Systems & Societies
name: IB ESS
about: IB Environmental Systems & Societies teaching-hour plan. Hours from the IB guide; lesson durations share each topic's hours. Built by lessongen/ib_plan.py.
source: IB ESS guide, first assessment 2026 (topic hours from the guide; subtopic hours shared by number of understandings, except topic 1 where the guide gives them).

lessons.title: Perspectives, the influences that shape them, and values in environmental communication
Values surveys, worldviews and environmental value systems: technocentric, anthropocentric and ecocentric
How environmental perspectives change over time, and the history of the environmental movement
Systems, the systems approach, storages and flows, and transfers versus transformations
Open and closed systems, the Earth as a system and the Gaia hypothesis, and systems at different scales
Negative feedback and Daisyworld, stable equilibrium, and positive feedback
Tipping points, new stable states such as eutrophication, and the uses and limits of models
Emergent properties, resilience, and how diversity, storage size and human activity affect resilience
Sustainability, its three pillars, strong and weak models, and environmental and social sustainability
Economic sustainability, sustainable development, collapse of the Newfoundland cod fishery, and GDP versus green GDP
Environmental justice, inequality and access, scales of sustainability, and sustainability indicators
Ecological footprints, carbon and water footprints, and biocapacity
Citizen science, the uses and limits of sustainability models, and the UN Sustainable Development Goals
Planetary boundaries, doughnut economics and the circular economy
Levels of organisation in the biosphere, species, classification and identifying organisms
Populations, distribution, abiotic factors and limits of tolerance, and the niche
Interactions between populations, carrying capacity, and density-dependent regulation by negative feedback
J-shaped and S-shaped population curves, removing limiting factors, and human carrying capacity
Sampling strategies, random quadrats for non-mobile organisms, and mark–release–recapture with the Lincoln index
Communities, habitats, ecosystems as open systems, and sustainability as a natural property of ecosystems
Ecosystem tipping points, keystone species, and the crossed biosphere integrity boundary
Clades, cladograms and how traditional taxonomic ranks relate to evolutionary divergence
Fundamental and realized niches, r- and K-strategists, and using classification and niches to assess human impacts
Energy and matter in ecosystems: conservation of energy, and photosynthesis as the entry point for energy
Producers, cellular respiration, heat loss and the inefficiency of energy transformations
Consumers, food chains and trophic levels, and the loss of energy and matter at each step
Gross and net productivity, the ten per cent rule, food webs and measuring biomass
Ecological pyramids, bioaccumulation and biomagnification, microplastics, and human disruption of energy and matter flows
Autotrophs and heterotrophs, photoautotrophs and chemoautotrophs, and primary productivity
Secondary productivity, net primary productivity as the base of food chains, and maximum sustainable yield
Higher sustainable yields at lower trophic levels, ecological efficiency, and entropy in ecosystems
Biogeochemical cycles, stores, sinks and sources, and the stores and flows of the carbon cycle
Carbon sequestration, ecosystems as stores, sinks or sources, fossil fuels, and agricultural systems in the carbon cycle
Ocean uptake of CO₂, ocean acidification and its effects, and measures to reduce human impacts on the carbon cycle
Carbon in the lithosphere: limestone formed by corals and molluscs, and the formation of coal, oil and gas
Methanogenic bacteria, the atmospheric lifetime of methane, and the stores of the nitrogen cycle
Bacteria in the nitrogen cycle: fixation, nitrification, denitrification in anaerobic soils, mutualism with legumes, and nitrogen flows
Human changes to the nitrogen cycle, the Haber process, the crossed nitrogen boundary, and global cooperation on nitrogen
Climate and weather, biomes, the abiotic factors that set biome distribution, and the characteristics of biome groups
The tricellular model of atmospheric circulation, ocean heat transport, and biome shifts with global warming
Three general climate types and their biomes, why predicted biomes may not develop, and the El Niño–Southern Oscillation
Effects of El Niño and La Niña on marine productivity, tropical cyclones, and warming oceans and cyclone intensity

topics.name: Zonation, succession and change in ecosystems

lessons.title: Zonation along environmental gradients, transects, succession, and seral stages leading to a climax community
Primary and secondary succession, changes in energy, productivity, diversity and soil during succession, and resilience to disturbance
Factors shaping succession: climate, bedrock, fire, weather and consumers, and net productivity through succession
r- and K-strategists in pioneer and climax communities, debates about the climax concept, and plagioclimax communities
Biodiversity at habitat, species and genetic levels, and how each level supports ecosystem resilience
Biodiversity arising through evolution, and natural selection: its conditions and long-term change
Speciation through isolation and divergence, and species diversity as richness plus evenness
Calculating Simpson's reciprocal index to compare species diversity, and using biodiversity knowledge in conservation
How mutation and sexual reproduction increase genetic diversity, and the mechanisms of reproductive isolation
The uneven distribution of biodiversity and tropical hotspots, human-altered selection pressures, and artificial selection
The age of Earth and the fossil record, the geologic time scale, and mass extinctions followed by rapid speciation
The Anthropocene as a proposed epoch, and the marks human activity will leave in the geological record
Direct and indirect human threats to biodiversity, multiple interacting impacts, and invasive alien species
The IUCN Red List and its criteria, and how conservation status guides priorities
Case studies of an extinct, a critically endangered and a recovered species, and the tragedy of the commons
Threats to tropical biodiversity hotspots, and the identification of Key Biodiversity Areas
Conflicts between exploitation, development and conservation in Key Biodiversity Areas, and Indigenous land management
Conservation and environmental justice, and extinction rates beyond the planetary threshold
Arguments for preserving biodiversity, in situ and ex situ conservation, and mixed approaches using flagship and keystone species
The Convention on Biological Diversity, protecting or actively managing habitats, and designing effective reserves
Rewilding through keystone species and connectivity, reversing biodiversity decline within planetary limits, and values in conservation choices
Factors in the success of conservation organisations, and rewilding as positive feedback that restores stable ecosystems
Benefits and limits of rewilding, assessing conservation success at three levels, and ecotourism
Solar radiation and gravity as drivers of the water cycle, its stores and flows, and the relative sizes of water stores
Hydrological flows, human alteration of the water cycle, and flow diagrams to show steady states and sustainable harvest rates
Unique properties of water, oceans as a carbon sink, acidification and long-term sediment storage, and the density maximum at 4 °C
Stratification and the thermocline, intensifying stratification, upwelling, and thermohaline circulation
Water security, factors affecting access, growing demand, and ways to increase supply
Physical and economic water scarcity, domestic water conservation, water-efficient food production, and mitigation strategies in named countries
The freshwater planetary boundary, water governance, water footprints, and citizen science in water management
Water stress beyond quantity, the 1 700 m³ threshold, and how causes of water stress depend on socio-economic context
Transboundary water disputes, industrial water strategies and their environmental costs, and unequal access to water and sanitation
Producers in aquatic food webs, human use of aquatic organisms, rising demand, and destructive harvesting methods
Fishery collapse such as Grand Banks cod, maximum sustainable yield and quotas, and threats from climate change and acidification
Policy and consumer choices, marine protected areas, and aquaculture and its environmental impacts
Productivity, stratification and nutrient loading, stock assessment, and the risks of harvesting at MSY
Recovery of overexploited species through cooperation, coastal state regulation and the high seas, and the ethics of harvesting marine mammals
Sources and impacts of water pollution, marine plastics, water quality indicators, and biochemical oxygen demand
Eutrophication: nutrient inputs, the sequence to oxygen depletion, impacts on ecosystem services, and management at three levels
Types of water pollutants, toxic algal blooms, and the spread of hypoxic and anoxic waters
Sewage treatment stages and equitable access, indicator species, and biotic indices such as the Trent index
Water quality indices, WHO drinking-water guidelines and national standards, and individual and citizen action against pollution
Soil as a dynamic system, its components, the development of soil horizons, and inputs to soil
Soil outputs, transfers and transformations, and systems flow diagrams for soil
How soil supports plants, soil as habitat for biodiversity, and decomposers recycling elements
Soil texture, how texture affects primary productivity, and soils as carbon sinks, stores or sources
Classifying soils by profile, O A B C horizons and their loss under intensive farming, topsoil vulnerability, and soil-forming factors
Particle size and cation-exchange capacity, measuring soil properties, and soil carbon release and tipping points
Finite land and a growing population, land use and marginalised groups, food production, distribution and waste, and how soils and climate shape farming
Types of farming systems, traditional pastoralism and shifting cultivation, the Green Revolution, and synthetic fertilizers and alternatives
Soil conservation, plant-based diets and trophic levels, global strategies to cut waste, emissions and land expansion, and food security
Contrasting agricultural choices shaped by soils and climate, alternative farming approaches, and regenerative agriculture and permaculture
High-tech greenhouses and vertical farms, diet sustainability and food miles, and traditional wild harvesting
Testing claims about low-productivity sustainable systems against global food needs, and why malnutrition and famine are about distribution and quality
The atmosphere as the boundary of the biosphere and its life-supporting composition, and differential heating driving tricellular circulation
Greenhouse gases and aerosols absorbing and re-emitting infrared radiation, and the natural and enhanced greenhouse effects
The atmosphere as a dynamic system, thinning with altitude and the lapse rate, and Milankovitch cycles
Global warming moving Earth beyond the Quaternary glacial–interglacial pattern, and the co-evolution of life and the atmosphere
Climate defined by temperature and precipitation, the rise in anthropogenic CO₂ since 1950, and proxy evidence linking CO₂ and temperature
Human emissions enhancing the greenhouse effect, ecosystem impacts and biome shifts, and societal impacts that vary with scale and socio-economic conditions
Feedback diagrams for climate change and the energy balance, the crossed climate planetary boundary, and differing perspectives on climate change
Direct and proxy climate data, climate models and hindcasting, and scenarios predicting impacts such as sea-level rise and precipitation change
Climate tipping points, tipping cascades, and climate justice: differing responsibility and vulnerability
The need for global action, decarbonisation and carbon neutrality, and mitigation strategies
Adaptation through structural and non-structural strategies, and National Adaptation Programmes of Action
Government and non-government responses, the UNFCCC, IPCC and COP summits, and IPCC emission scenarios
Technology and smart cities in mitigation, and barriers to climate action
Geoengineering: treating symptoms not causes and its drawbacks, and how stakeholders shape individual climate perspectives
Differing views on climate action by age, development and economic interests, and the tragedy of the commons requiring international cooperation
The solar spectrum and UV radiation, why shorter UV wavelengths are more dangerous, and how stratospheric ozone absorbs UV
Damage by UV to phytoplankton, DNA, skin and eyes, the natural balance of ozone formation and destruction, and ozone-depleting substances
Effects of increased UVB, the Montreal Protocol as a success of international cooperation, and keeping within the ozone planetary boundary
How ODSs release chlorine and fluorine that break down ozone, and polar spring ozone depletion from unique stratospheric conditions
HFCs as ozone-safe but potent greenhouse gases and the Kigali Amendment, and air conditioning, energy use and alternatives
Natural resources, natural capital and natural income, and natural capital as a model that views nature as a resource
Ecosystem services, renewable and non-renewable resources, types of value, and how the value of natural capital changes
Managing natural capital within regeneration and absorption limits, resource security, and the factors behind resource choices
Management and intervention strategies for natural capital, and the SDGs as a framework for sustainable resource management
Environmental impact assessments, differences in EIA guidance between countries, and public participation in EIAs
Renewable resources extracted or processed unsustainably, and short-term economic interests depleting resources such as fish and forests
Resource insecurity, development and conflict, improving resource security, and globalisation and national resource security
Renewable and non-renewable energy sources, rising global energy consumption, and the sustainability and environmental costs of energy sources
Factors in national energy choices, storage for intermittent renewables, and conservation and efficiency to reduce import dependence
Energy security as affordable and reliable supply, and the global economy's reliance on finite fossil fuel reserves
Nuclear power: low carbon with mining, thermal, accident and waste concerns, and battery minerals: lithium, cobalt and rare earths
Classifying waste by source and type, the composition of solid domestic waste, and factors affecting waste volume and composition
Distant impacts and waste exports, pollution as input exceeding breakdown, and why prevention beats restoration
Disposal options and trade-offs, promoting sustainable waste management through policy and education, and circular economy principles
Population inputs and outputs, demographic measures (fertility, life expectancy, doubling time, natural increase), and UN projections
Pro-natalist and anti-natalist policies, development policies that indirectly change population, age–sex pyramids, and the demographic transition model
Rapid population growth and pressure on planetary boundaries, and dependency ratio and population momentum from age–sex pyramids
Population patterns in two countries at different DTM stages, and environmental migration driven by climate change and degradation
Urban ecosystems, urban versus rural areas, the city as an interconnected system, and urbanisation
Rural–urban migration and push and pull factors, suburbanisation and urban sprawl, and environmental impacts of urban expansion
Urban planning and stakeholders, sustainable urban planning, and ecological urban planning that treats cities as ecosystems
Compact cities, mixed land use and social mix to reduce sprawl and improve equity, and circular economy and doughnut models in cities
Green architecture: environmentally friendly materials, design and practices
Urban air pollutants, natural and human sources, fossil fuel combustion, and strategies to reduce urban air pollution
Formation of acid deposition from NOₓ and SO₂, its impacts on ecosystems, buildings and health, and management strategies
Photochemical smog formation from primary to secondary pollutants, and how sunlight, low wind and temperature inversions intensify it
Effects of tropospheric ozone on plants, eyes, lungs and materials, and the economic, healthcare and equity costs of ozone pollution
What laws are, environmental law and its aims, and how environmental law supports justice but faces lobbying
Effectiveness of environmental law, environmental constitutionalism, and local, national and international levels of law
International law for transboundary pollution and shared resources, conventions and protocols, and institutions created by agreements
International courts and tribunals, legal personhood of natural entities, and combining legal and economic strategies
Economics and environmental economics, market failure and externalities, and the polluter-pays principle
Greenwashing, the tragedy of the commons and property rights, environmental accounting, and non-use values estimated by surveys
Ecological economics, valuing ecosystem services and compensating resource-rich countries, and economic growth and GDP
Growth-focused economics ignoring degradation, growth both raising pollution and funding protection, and eco-economic decoupling
Degrowth and zero growth, the difficulties of dismantling growth-dependent systems, and circular and doughnut economics as ecological economics
Ethics, environmental ethics, and how views of the human–nature relationship produce different ethical frameworks
Instrumental and intrinsic value, how they can coexist, and moral standing
Three traditional ethical approaches: virtue ethics, consequentialist ethics and rights-based ethics
Rights-based ethics and contested rights, the appeal-to-nature fallacy, and the converging environmental and social justice movements
